 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, November 6, 2026: Check Latest Rates In Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru

 Mumbai, November 6: Retail fuel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals. Petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel rates stood at Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 Oil prices rose for a second consecutive session on Friday, recovering further from a steep selloff earlier in the week as fresh attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East revived concerns over supply disruptions. However, both major crude benchmarks remained on course for weekly losses of around 12%, with expectations of a possible de-escalation of the Iran war continuing to weigh on prices.   
 Brent crude futures gained 2 percent to $100.3 per barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures advanced 1.5 percent to $91.8 per barrel. Both contracts had also settled higher in the previous session.   
 Despite the two-day recovery, Brent was headed for a weekly decline of around 12 percent, while WTI was set to shed approximately 12.1 percent. The losses follow a dramatic correction earlier in the week, when crude prices fell 8 percent on Wednesday alone, touching their lowest levels in two months.   
 The sharp decline followed the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, which gave the party control of both chambers of Congress. Investors interpreted the result as potentially increasing political pressure on US President Donald Trump to pursue an end to the US-Israeli war against Iran, now in its ninth month.   
 The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough raised expectations that restrictions on energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz could eventually ease, improving the outlook for global crude supplies.   
 However, the recovery in oil prices over the past two sessions suggests that traders remain cautious about assuming a quick resolution to the conflict.   
 Fresh attacks on commercial vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday have renewed concerns about the security of Middle Eastern oil shipments.   
 Iran reported on Thursday that three additional tankers had come under attack in the Strait of Hormuz. Data from the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) also indicated that incidents involving tankers remained close to record levels.   
 The Strait of Hormuz is a critical shipping route for global energy supplies, and disruption to vessel movements through the passage could constrain crude shipments from the Middle East.   
 Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at ANZ, said traders viewed Wednesday’s sharp selloff as excessive. He noted that Iran continued to exercise control over the Strait of Hormuz, with overall shipping flows through the passage running at less than 60 percent of capacity.   
 For India, which depends heavily on imported crude to meet its energy requirements, the sharp weekly decline in international oil prices offers some relief on the import bill, inflation and currency front.   
 However, continued uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict and tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz could limit further downside in crude prices. Investors will closely monitor geopolitical developments and the prospects of a diplomatic resolution for cues on the next direction of the oil market.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in your city, including Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Friday, November 6, with no revision reported in retail fuel rates. In New Delhi, petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 111.21 per litre and those in Kolkata paid Rs 113.51 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, petrol was retailing at Rs 107.76 per litre in Chennai and Rs 111.68 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad continued to have one of the highest petrol prices among major cities at Rs 116.15 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram was at Rs 115.49 per litre.   
 In northern India, petrol was priced at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurugram and Rs 101.96 per litre in Noida. Chandigarh recorded a rate of Rs 101.54 per litre, while Jaipur and Lucknow reported prices of Rs 113.19 and Rs 101.89 per litre, respectively.   
 Among other state capitals, petrol was retailing at Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 113.37 per litre in Patna. The unchanged retail prices come amid fluctuations in international crude oil markets, with global benchmark Brent crude remaining an important factor influencing India’s fuel-price outlook.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian metropolitan cities and state capitals on Friday, November 6, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 97.83 per litre and those in Kolkata paid Rs 99.82 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, diesel retailed at Rs 99.55 per litre in Chennai and Rs 99.56 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad recorded one of the highest rates at Rs 104.23 per litre, while diesel was marginally more expensive in Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 104.40 per litre.   
 In northern India, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurugram and Rs 95.44 per litre in Noida. Chandigarh had a comparatively lower rate of Rs 89.47 per litre, while Jaipur and Lucknow reported prices of Rs 98.25 and Rs 95.36 per litre, respectively.   
 Among other state capitals, diesel was retailing at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 99.36 per litre in Patna. Despite fluctuations in international crude oil prices, domestic diesel rates remained steady, with consumers seeing no change in their fuel bills.
